title: Review: Purity, formulations and chromatography; Identification of common gases
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.8.1-c07, 4.8.1-c14, 4.8.2-c07, 4.8.2-c12. Clues: 4.8.1-c07 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.8.1-c14 written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.8.2-c07 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.8.2-c12 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.8.1-q20, 4.8.1-q21, 4.8.1-q22, 4.8.1-q23, 4.8.1-q24, 4.8.1-q10, 4.8.1-q19, 4.8.2-q01, 4.8.2-q03, 4.8.2-q05, 4.8.1-q09, 4.8.1-q18. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Formulation
items.clue: A mixture that has been designed as a useful product.

items.label: Rf value
items.clue: Distance moved by the substance divided by distance moved by the solvent.

items.label: limewater
items.clue: An aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, used as the test reagent for carbon dioxide.

items.label: bleached
items.clue: The colour of the litmus paper is removed so that the paper turns white; this is the positive result for chlorine.

questions.stem: When finding an Rf value from a chromatogram, how is the distance moved by the substance measured?

options.text: From the bottom edge of the paper to the spot
From the pencil line to the top of the spot
From the pencil line to the spot's centre
From the pencil line to the very top of the paper

questions.explanation: The specification defines the distance as the centre of the spot measured from the origin.

questions.stem: On a chromatogram a spot has moved 3.6 cm from the pencil line and the solvent has moved 9.0 cm. What is the Rf value of the spot?

options.text: 5.4 cm, the difference of the two
2.5, worked out as 9.0 cm / 3.6 cm
0.40, worked out as 3.6 cm / 9.0 cm
0.40 cm, since Rf is a distance

questions.explanation: R_f= (distance moved by substance) / (distance moved by solvent) = 3.6 / 9.0 = 0.40.

questions.stem: A spot moved 2.7 cm and the solvent moved 5.9 cm. The calculator shows 0.457627 for the Rf value. How should the answer be given?

options.text: 0.46, matching the two significant figures measured
0.4576, since the extra digits make it more accurate
0.457627, exactly as the calculator displays it
0.5, rounded to just one significant figure

questions.explanation: An answer is quoted to no more significant figures than the measurements it came from.

questions.stem: In Required practical 6, why is the start line on the chromatography paper drawn in pencil?

options.text: Ink would react with the solvent to make a new dye
Pencil is easier to see against the coloured dyes
Pencil holds the spots in place on the line
Pencil does not dissolve and move up the paper

questions.explanation: Pencil is insoluble in the solvent, so the line stays put instead of separating into spots of its own.

questions.stem: Why must the solvent in the beaker start below the pencil line on the paper?

options.text: Otherwise the paper would sink to the beaker's base
Otherwise the spots dissolve into the solvent
Otherwise the solvent front would end up uneven
Otherwise the solvent would rise too fast up the paper

questions.explanation: Solvent above the line washes the samples off the paper instead of carrying them up it.

questions.stem: A student is given information about four substances. Which one is a formulation?

options.text: A paint with pigment, binder and solvent in fixed amounts
Sea water, a mixture of water and many different dissolved salts
Distilled water sold in bottles for topping up an iron
Nitrogen taken from air and used to fill food packets

questions.explanation: Components with particular purposes, mixed in measured quantities to make a useful product, define a formulation.

questions.stem: A chromatogram is run on a food colouring. Which result shows that the colouring is impure?

options.text: It gives a single spot, proving it is pure
The colouring separates into more than one spot
Its spot is bigger than the spot of the reference dye
Its Rf value differs from the reference dye's value

questions.explanation: The compounds in a mixture separate into different spots, so several spots show the sample is impure.

questions.stem: A burning splint is held at the open end of a test tube of an unknown gas. Which observation shows that the gas is hydrogen?

options.text: The gas burns rapidly with a pop sound
The splint relights, burning brightly
The splint is put out straight away
The gas burns with a steady flame

questions.explanation: This is the stated result of the hydrogen test: hydrogen burns rapidly with a pop sound.

questions.stem: A glowing splint is inserted into a test tube of gas and the splint relights. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: The gas is carbon dioxide, as it relights splints
The gas is oxygen, as it relights the splint
The relighting shows the gas is burning itself
The gas is hydrogen, as it relights splints

questions.explanation: The splint relights in oxygen, so relighting identifies the gas as oxygen.

questions.stem: Limewater is used in the test for carbon dioxide. What is limewater?

options.text: An aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide
An aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide
An aqueous calcium carbonate solution
An aqueous calcium chloride solution

questions.explanation: The specification defines limewater as an aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide.

questions.stem: Why are the components of a formulation mixed in carefully measured quantities?

options.text: So the mixture becomes one pure compound as it is stirred
So the components all react and leave no waste behind
So the product has exactly the properties it was designed to have
They need not be measured; only the ingredients matter

questions.explanation: The quantities are part of the design, and the proportions are what give the product its required properties.

questions.stem: A dye is held strongly by the paper and dissolves only slightly in the solvent. On the chromatogram this dye will

options.text: travel with the solvent front, as dissolved dyes do
stay on the line, unable to enter the paper
move furthest of all, being the lightest one
move only a short way up, giving a low Rf value

questions.explanation: Strong attraction to the stationary phase keeps the dye near the origin, so its Rf value is small.
